question: what actually clears the fold cache that §CL's conclusion depends on, how long have the F3/F4 cache files already survived it, what fraction of executed epochs is observable at all, and is M1's fold-wise epoch drop an artefact of degenerate runs?

policy_line_fields.note: tmpfiles.d columns are Type Path Mode User Group Age Argument, so the age field is index 5 and NOT index 4. The first version of this probe read parts[4] and published age='root', which is the group column -- a wrong value in the one field the whole conclusion turns on, since age '-' is what makes the daily --clean a no-op here.

tmp_policy.age_field_meaning: '-' means no age-based cleanup, so systemd-tmpfiles --clean deletes nothing here on account of age
tmp_policy.reading: a sharp cutoff at the boot instant is what an empty-at-boot policy produces; zero survivors older than boot is the evidence, and the daily --clean timer cannot be what clears /tmp because the age field is '-'

cache_survival.atime_disclosure: reading a parquet footer updates atime under this filesystem's relatime mount option, so the §CJ/§CK/§CL probes changed the atime of the 12 files they inspected. mtime is unchanged on all 46 files and none was modified after 09-09, so content is intact; the extractor depends only on path existence and file content, and with age '-' the cleaner consults no timestamp, so nothing in the pipeline reads atime.

version_retention.reading: the database retains old versions rather than replacing them, so a cold re-assembly inside the SAME process -- which re-filters by the SAME pinned versions (filter_current, walk_forward_common.py:150-155) -- would reproduce the same rows provided those versions are still present
version_retention.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: this covers universe_daily on 20 days (2024-12-20 .. 2025-01-17) only. It does NOT evidence retention for factor_daily or label_daily, nor for the 2017-2025 training years. So 'a cache deletion without a restart is recoverable' is supported for one of three tables on a 20-day window and must not be cited as a general guarantee.
version_retention.restart_is_the_dangerous_case: current_versions sorts by published_at and lets later rows overwrite earlier ones, i.e. it picks the NEWEST published version per partition. A restarted process therefore pins whatever is newest at the new start time, which need not match 09-13's snapshot -- and --resume restores search records, not that in-memory snapshot.

M1.scope: grid runs only (final-refit runs excluded, matching §CJ's phase split)

M2.scope: grid runs only (final-refit runs excluded, matching §CJ's phase split)

observability.reading: a checkpoint is written only on strict improvement (trainer.py:110-116), so every epoch a run executed AFTER its peak leaves no trace. The observable fraction of executed epochs is this low, and runs with exactly one checkpoint have nothing but epoch 1 on the record. Every training-dynamics statistic in this pack (§BO.9's peak spread, §CA/§CB's peak-basis variance decomposition, §CI's epochs/run trend, §CJ's cap scan, §CK's four-fold pattern) is computed from peaks, which is the right quantity for 'where did it converge' but carries no information about the shape of the decline after the peak.

order_flip_between_mean_and_central_mass.what: does F3 or F4 have the longer TYPICAL run? The mean and the central mass disagree, so any comparison of these two folds must state its basis
order_flip_between_mean_and_central_mass.cause: F3 is bimodal (30 runs at peak<=2 AND 13 at peak>=20, p90 31, max 33) while F4 is uniformly low (23 at peak<=2 but only 2 at peak>=20, p90 15, max 20), so F3's mean is lifted by its upper tail while its central mass sits below F4's
order_flip_between_mean_and_central_mass.consequence: §CI's 1.647x growth and §CK.2's 'non-monotone, peaking at F2' are both mean-basis statements and both hold on that basis, but neither discloses that F3 and F4 swap places on the median basis

fourth_candidate_excluded.verdict: REJECTED as the explanation: holding the peak==1 share at F1's 3.7% removes only 7.9% of the drop. The real change is a whole-distribution leftward shift -- the median falls 15 -> 3 -> 4 while the 25%-trimmed mean falls only 12.76 -> 4.76 -> 5.49 and the raw mean 13.27 -> 9.09 -> 6.96. So §CK.8's open question loses a fourth candidate (degenerate-run influx) and keeps three excluded (config mix, panel size, validation signal strength), with no cause established.

synthetic_impossible_run.reading: the guard is on n_ck <= peak, NOT on the ratio: this impossible input would have produced 60%, an ordinary-looking number, so an out-of-range check would not have caught it. The ratio itself is uninformative about the bug.

conclusion.what_clears_the_cache: a BOOT, not elapsed time and not the daily cleaner: tmp.conf uses type D (create-and-REMOVE) with age '-' (no age-based cleanup), and the boot unit runs --create --remove --boot while the daily timer runs only --clean
conclusion.evidence_of_boot_clearing: 0 /tmp entries predate the last boot (2026-08-11 15:41:07), with 13 created inside the boot hour -- a sharp cutoff
conclusion.so_CL7b_should_read: 'the cache is deleted' means 'the machine reboots' (or a manual rm), not 'time passes' or 'the daily cleaner runs'. Over the ~2-3 weeks M2 still needs, the operative question is whether this host reboots, which is a much more specific thing to watch than /tmp hygiene.
conclusion.fourth_candidate_for_CK8: rejected (explains only 7.9% of the F2->F4 drop)

side_effect_disclosed: atime of the 12 inspected cache files was updated to 2026-09-18 20:17:44 by the §CJ/§CK/§CL probes reading their footers; mtime and content unchanged
